label: input token d at one of the first three original positions (t<=2)
explanation: Fires whenever the input token is the letter d at original positions 0, 1 or 2. On dev it fires on about 100% of those steps (precision 1.0, recall 0.9999). How strongly it fires depends on position: at t=0 it is near its maximum (about 2.0), at t=1 it is roughly 0.65-0.72 of max, and at t=2 it is roughly 0.2-0.3 of max. Equal step counts at each position give mass shares of 0.52, 0.35 and 0.13. It does not fire on d at positions 3 and later, on any other token, on the delimiter, or in the copy phase, where the model outputs d as an input fed back. The only exceptions are 6 stray copy-phase activations.

issues: None of the claims could be refuted. On the test split, precision is 1.0, recall 0.99976, F1 0.99988 and mass recall 0.99999. There are 0 false positives.

The dev profile matches the explanation. Of the d steps that are active, 100% are at t=0..2 (16601/16688/16676 active steps out of 500k each). There are 0 activations on any other token and 0 on the delimiter. The copy phase has only 6 activations. Mass shares by t are 0.518, 0.351 and 0.132.
The magnitude falloff is consistent with the mass ratios: 0.35/0.52 is about 0.67 and 0.13/0.52 is about 0.25, with a similar number of activations at each position. The max is 2.02.

The 12 test misses are copy-phase steps where d is read back in from the model's own output for a d that was in positions 0..2. Each is about 0.02-0.04 of max and together they hold 0.0% of the mass. That is scattered noise, not a systematic class.
Minor wording point: the explanation's 'only 6 stray copy-phase activations' is a dev count (test has about 12). This makes no material difference.
